author: jsign
content:
This is mainly a scope decision of 8025 reg proof being optional, given that there are other prover killers that doesn't make relying on proof being unsound anyway (e.g. bytecode code-chunking) is needed anyway.
We wanted to make 8025 as simple as possible to upstream a lot of existing work with the least amount of friction for EL/CLs/specs.

Recursive proving and benefits/implications for CL syncing is definitely somthing that isn't discarded, but not critical for getting most of the benefits of 8025 being upstreamed. We'll definitely work on recursive proving since that's necessary for proper CL-sycning; can def happen in 8025 if ACD is okay with it (since this broadens the scope of the EIP) or we can simply keep it as a further iteration more into mandatory proofs.

author: jsign
content:
Mainly the argument here is that 8025 should be considered as something simple to be proposed for H* both for CL, EL and specs -- if not prob we're making it harder to be CFIed. 😅 
The north start is quite clear that we keep iterating on the recursive proof style for proofs.
